event_model_payload.headline: Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA6) – We NEED To Talk About Carjacking
event_model_payload.summary:
Rockstar's next GTA game for the PS5 and Xbox is only a few months away, and the team is dramatically shaking up the formula.

This week we're talking about carjacking and how it changes nearly every aspect of Grand Theft Auto as we know it.

event_model_payload.headline: GTA 6 Is Completely Changing How You Steal Cars
event_model_payload.summary:
Carjacking in Grand Theft Auto games has been, as the title denotes, a staple of the series. Up until now, it's largely been the same. While there have been more details and animations added over the years, the premise has remained that you'll walk up to a car, press Y or Triangle, throw the driver out, get in and drive away. If the car was parked, you'd execute the same button press to smash the window and steal it. With GTA 6, carjacking is getting a complete overhaul. Here, we've got all of the information we know so far on how to steal cars in GTA 6.

There are two ways to steal a car: taking one that's stationary, or taking one that someone's driving around in. However, there are more details that make GTA 6 feel more like true simulation gameplay now.

How to steal a parked car

As we saw in the GTA 6 extended look gameplay, when Jason approached a car, he had multiple options to choose from. The first option is a slim jim--a classic tool used to break into older vehicles. It slides down the window frame to adjust the lock, and in GTA 6, it seems like this is done via a lockpicking minigame. However, based on what we've heard so far, that won't work for every car. Depending on the year and model of the vehicle, you might not be able to use a slim jim.

However, newer and more expensive cars might not work with this method. On top of that, there are trackers, meaning that the police can track your location when you steal a car. This changes the whole carjacking aspect of Grand Theft Auto. Normally, if you'd steal a car, you might catch some heat; maybe a nearby police officer sees you and follows you, but it's pretty easy to get away cleanly. This time, that isn't the case.

If you do want to get away cleanly, you need an item to disable the tracking device. It seems like that item, along with the slim jim, is not something you start out with, meaning you'll need to progress through the story or complete side objectives to obtain them.

Another interesting thing about the tracker is that apparently if you drive fast enough, the cops won't be able to track you. That adds an extra element of tension, because if you slow down and try to play it safe, they'll know exactly where you are and you'll need to get moving right away.

How to steal occupied vehicles

In some cases, driven vehicles aren't locked, so you'll be able to just walk up and open the door. It seems like there's a quick time minigame to complete, which will wrestle the driver out of the car, and then you can drive away. If there is a passenger, they will also try to prevent you from stealing the car. However, just because you steal a car doesn't mean the cops can't track you--the tracker is still there and you will need to find a way to disable it.

Vehicle security and impound lots

How do you know what kind of security a given car on the street has? The app Waink allows you to scan vehicles, and it'll tell you the security systems on board as well as how much it'll cost to register it as your own vehicle.

One other interesting detail about registered vehicles that was in one of TGG's videos is that if you ditch one of your own cars while you are wanted, the police will set up a perimeter around your car so that if you return to it, in theory, they will be waiting for you. If you wait too long, they will impound it. This leads to some interesting gameplay implications. Perhaps you'll have to sneak into the impound lot to retrieve it, or if you have the money, you could show up and pay the fee before driving off.

There's certainly something deeper going on with the Grand Theft Auto mechanics we've known for years. Supposedly, when you start the game you won't have access to a lot of these tools. You won't be able to instantly steal cars; you'll have to progress to that point. It seems like better vehicles will slowly be introduced throughout the game.

If you want better vehicles, you'll have to work for them, whether that's through stealing or more legitimate means. This also leads to interesting repercussions when it comes to robberies and other activities. You'll want a fast getaway car--previously, you could just acquire the nearest suitable one, but in GTA 6 you'll have to plan ahead. If a nearby car is parked, you might not have the equipment to stealthily steal it. Even if you do, maybe you don't have the gear to remove the tracker, which will bring more heat on you.

This means that robberies need to be pre-planned. Perhaps Jason or Lucia will be on watch with a vehicle, so the other character can run out, hop in, and drive away. Maybe you'll choose a vehicle as your getaway car early on, steal it, park it nearby, and then complete the robbery knowing you have a method of escape.

GTA 6 is bringing about many more changes for the series. While many thought Jason and Lucia would be in a romantic relationship, it turns out that's not actually necessary. The game has also removed the need to button mash to sprint--something I've been desperate for.

event_model_payload.headline: I’m Begging You To Stop Obsessing Over Player Numbers And Just Enjoy Games
event_model_payload.summary:
Horror fans are confused. Every time a licensed multiplayer horror game gets brought up, two things tend to happen: commenters wonder if it can dethrone Dead by Daylight, and they speculate that the game will shut down quickly. It's happening again today, as I've recently published my Halloween review. Comments on YouTube and in Discord servers are already repeating the sentiments I've seen for many years now.

"Probably be dead in six months to a year because no one can live aside DBD."

"It will be dead within a month like the rest."

"The real question is, will it go the way of Evil Dead, Friday the 13th, and Texas Chain Saw, and not touch Dead by Daylight?"

I view this response as a kind of mass hallucination. This obsession over a game's health and future prospects is a widespread problem in a number of genres right now, but it's been especially irksome in the multiplayer horror space, where people rely on points that may feel true but don't prove accurate upon closer inspection.

I've played nearly every licensed multiplayer horror game, like those named above and others, like Killer Klowns and Predator: Hunting Grounds. For the past decade, Hollywood licensors have been increasingly interested in adapting their intellectual properties to games, and with each new one revealed, there's an expectation among players and onlookers that they will die off, failing to topple the titan of the genre, Dead by Daylight.

It's true that Dead by Daylight remains in a league of its own in terms of its community size. What I find absurd, though, is that these other games are seeking to usurp Behaviour Interactive's decade-long success story. Not one of these games seems to have aspirations or expectations of replacing DBD. Ultimately, they're very different things, and these other adaptations are only looking to earn their place alongside DBD.

In some important ways, Dead by Daylight is closer to Fortnite than it is Friday the 13th or Halloween. To date, DBD has brought more than 40 killers, many of them from licensed horror movies and shows, to its one-size-fits-all framework. Except in cases of limited-time modes, DBD is always about four players sneaking around dozens of different maps, repairing generators, avoiding being hooked, and escaping off the map before the killer ends them. It's a fun game I literally play every night, but it doesn't offer a bespoke experience. Whether you're playing as Ghostface, Leatherface, Pinhead, or Chucky, your job is to prevent survivors from fixing generators and opening the exit doors. 

It makes for a great, highly competitive gameplay loop, but it doesn't make sense in any of these killers' original universes. Freddy Krueger is obsessed with invading the dreams of Springwood kids. Outside of DBD, he's never been seen guarding generators to prevent Steve from Stranger Things and Detective Tapp from Saw from powering the exit doors. Again, it's a wonderful game, but the thing it lacks most is authenticity for any one slasher or other horror franchise. It's never the point for games like Texas Chain Saw Massacre to try and take the crown from DBD. What these other games want to do is capture the spirit of their source material. That's a goal that can, and does, coexist with DBD quite peacefully.

It's true that some players who enjoy games like this only have enough time in a day to play one, and maybe on many days for many players, that's DBD. But so far, hardly any of the other licensed asymmetrical multiplayer horror games have had grand designs as live-service games. They get cosmetics and updates, sure, but most don't include things like daily or weekly check-in incentives, and when they have, they're more lax than DBD's full suite of live-service mechanics. They don't want to be your forever-game the way DBD does. They're different tastes, and I love the variety they collectively offer.

As prevalent and wrong-headed as that "DBD killer" narrative is, it's really secondary to the "dead game" narrative. Players like to predict that each one of these new licensed horror games will die off quickly, "like the rest," they say. But the truth is, history isn't on these doomsayers' side.

Friday the 13th died because of a legal drama that saw its rights change hands, and any ongoing deals based on it, such as IllFonic and Gun's multiplayer game, were forced to end. Suffice it to say, though this could happen again in theory, it would seem to be a rare case, perhaps never to be repeated. If that legal battle had never happened, I expect Jason would still be alive today.

In nearly every other case, games of this sort are doing fine. Not everything has to be the biggest game in the world. I worry players have become so obsessed with Steam player counts that they've stood in the way of their own fun. You can hop into a round of Killer Klowns, Texas Chain Saw Massacre, or Predator right now. While some are no longer adding new content, they're all in good shape, and I still enjoy rotating through them regularly. 

Players especially like to call out Texas Chain Saw Massacre as some sort of cautionary tale, saying that the developers failed to deliver on content promises, even though all they ever promised was to support the game with new updates as long as it made financial sense for the studios involved. That lasted about two years, which seems fine to me. If I paid $30 for a game and had a blast for two years, I'd call that getting my money's worth. 

The pushback against that seems born from the idea that every multiplayer game must now be both massive and ever-changing. Can't games just be fun for a while anymore? I don't want to see them go offline; don't get me wrong. But so long as they stay playable, why must they keep offering new things to do? It's like regular players now take their cues from the venture capitalists infecting every fandom with never-ending expectations to grow and prosper more than they did last week, last month, last year. It makes me want to scream: We have a bunch of fun video games based on some of the best horror movies ever made! 

I do admit, not every example supports my argument. I know of two horror games that went offline and were delisted: Evil Dead and Puppet Master. In the case of the former, I'd only note that I found it to be the least enjoyable of all those I've played. That doesn't mean I wanted it to be delisted, and the teams behind that decision, Saber and Boss Team, deserve criticism for taking it away like that. 

As for Puppet Master, I almost have to excuse that one. I'm neck-deep in this genre, and I nearly never knew it existed, only spotting it on Steam a short while before it got taken down. It seems it wasn't even on the map of players like me. I certainly wish I got to play it, and that others could do so whenever they wanted to, but to me these are exceptions to the rule. 

On the whole, horror multiplayer games are doing well. It feels like we've hardly scratched the surface of what other games can spring up from this trend--please, somebody make my Scream game with social deduction, whodunnit leanings. For now, Halloween is the latest of them, and yet another really fun one. I wish horror fans could experience these for what they are, rather than fold each of them into a bigger conversation about their financial prospects. I am literally Michael Myers, and I'm having a great time. That alone is worth celebrating.

event_model_payload.headline: Where To Find Lacra In The Blood Of Dawnwalker
event_model_payload.summary:
Are you looking for Lacra in The Blood of Dawnwalker? This fiendish vrakhiri--a potentially romanceable character at that--has been stalking her prey all over Vale Sangora. If you know the right people to ask, you might just learn of her whereabouts.

A Friend Like This - Where to find Lacra in Svartrau City

The quest where you find Lacra in The Blood of Dawnwalker is called A Friend Like This. It’s not available right from the get-go. Instead, you have to put in a bit of effort by heading to Svartrau City.

There, you’ll meet a benign vrakhiri named Vicho, who wants your help in solving a murder. You can learn about the details in our A Study in Crimson guide. After killing Doctor Simeon, Vicho will mention another vampire that’s roaming around the capital.

From the streets to the rooftops

If you check the journal entry for A Friend Like This, you’ll see that there are three spots in the northern part of the city that you need to check. Walk along the streets near the city’s gates and activate Focus Mode. You’ll see glowing objects, such as blood spatters, destroyed barrels, and fallen tiles.

Keep following your lead until you spot roof tiles that have been damaged. If it’s nighttime/you’re in vampire form, simply Shadowstep/Planeshift onto the roof. Traverse the buildings, all while using your Focus ability to search for more tiles. Eventually, you’ll reach a small house in a walled-off section of the city.

Follow the clues (left) until you reach Lacra's hideout (right).

Lacra boss fight

Your first meeting with Lacra in The Blood of Dawnwalker is actually a boss battle. Once you step inside the building, you’ll have a short conversation with Lacra, before she turns hostile. Be careful when fighting her since she has quick strikes with her claws. She can also transform into a wolf, leaping at you for a deadly bite.

Note: If you attempt to use Voracious Bite on Lacra, she’ll just elbow you in the face. You have to use other vampiric healing methods to stay alive.

The uriashi interrogation

After the bout, talk to Lacra once more until she addresses the uriashi in the room. You can spare the poor fella if you’d like:

  • “Gladly, but we’ll actually talk.”
  • “What happened? Tell me your side of the story.”
  • “You have my word.”
  • “I promise.”
  • “You’re not killing him.”

This concludes The Blood of Dawnwalker A Friend Like This quest. After this part, you’ll be able to travel to the hidden uriash village to the southwest. We discuss it in our Song of the Mountain guide. Oh, and don’t forget that Coen can romance Lacra as well.

event_model_payload.headline: Where To Find The Hidden Uriash Village In The Blood Of Dawnwalker
event_model_payload.summary:
Are you looking for the hidden Uriash Village in The Blood of Dawnwalker? This settlement is in a far-flung region that most humans can’t even reach. In fact, it will remain accessible to Coen unless you’re able to tackle some pre-requisite tasks.

Song of the Mountain - The Hidden Uriash Village

The hidden Uriash Village in The Blood of Dawnwalker, which is in the western corner of the map, can’t be visited under normal circumstances. If you attempt to climb up the mountainous area west of Rockfalls, a prompt will tell you that you’re not allowed to go any further, causing you to respawn some distance away.

To gain access to it, you must first meet a vampiress named Lacra. You can learn about all the info in our A Friend Like This guide.

After completing A Friend Like This, you’ll be able to speak with an uriash prisoner. Spare him and tell him that you’ll avoid killing the uriash in the village. This makes the Song of the Mountain quest appear in your journal. If you track it, you’ll see that your next task is to meet up with Lacra in Crown Rock. Since Lacra is a vrakhiri, you can only do this quest at night.

Traveling with Lacra

Here’s what you need to know about The Blood of Dawnwalker Song of the Mountain quest:

  • After talking to Lacra in Crown Rock, she’ll goad you into feeding on an unwary shepherd. Tell her that the experience is “an excellent one” to avoid offending her.
  • Continue along the mountain pass. If you see vertical cliff faces, use your Shadowstep and Planeshift to traverse the area.
  • At certain points, you have to fight wild animals, including wolves and bears.

Drink the blood of the shepherd (left) and slay some beasts (right).

The troublesome trolls

Save your game when you’re almost at the summit. That’s because the uriashi matriarch and her cohorts will appear. They'll start pelting Coen with rocks, all while Lacra insists that you need to make them pay for their insolence.

You’ll be presented with numerous dialogue options, and one mistake might lead to all-out hostilities. Here’s what we did to ensure a peaceful resolution:

  • “All right, fine.”
  • “Lacra, calm down.”
  • “Nobody needs to die.”
  • “Can we stop with the hostilities?”
  • “We’ve already proven it.”
  • “What more proof do you need?”
  • [Do nothing] - Twice.
  • “It’s clearly a test--go on.”
  • [Do nothing]

If you did it right, the uriashi matriarch, Bakr-Erga, will tell her warriors to stand down. She’ll then lead you to the settlement.

That does it for our guide on where to find the hidden Uriash Village in The Blood of Dawnwalker. The settlement itself has a fast travel shrine and several vendors--i.e. the matriarch sells almost every Witchcraft skill manual in the game.

From here, you can keep doing Lacra’s quests, until such time that you’re able to unlock her romance scene. You can also help the matriarch get her daughter back. We’ve got the details for you in our Ocha: The Heart Wants What It Wants guide.

event_model_payload.headline: How To Help Ocha In The Blood Of Dawnwalker – The Heart Wants What It Wants Guide
event_model_payload.summary:
Do you want to help Ocha in The Blood of Dawnwalker? The daughter of the uriash matriarch is somewhere in the capital, and she seems to have gotten into a bit of trouble. Our guide, which tackles A Mother’s Plea and The Heart Wants What It Wants, has all the info you need. We discuss everything from Ocha’s location and the memento that you need for a hex, right down to the responses that you need to pick to make Osha go back home or stay in the city.

In This Article
  • The Heart Wants What It Wants and Ocha story arc guide
    • Where to find Ocha in Svartrau City
    • How to enter Andrei’s hideout
    • Which of Andrei’s mementos should you steal: Cleaver, pendant, or ring?
    • How to save Nora
    • How to make Ocha go home or stay in the city
    • A Mother’s Plea: Conclusion and Ocha’s wares

The Heart Wants What It Wants and Ocha story arc guide

It’s going to be a while before you can help Ocha in The Blood of Dawnwalker. That’s because you need to do a few quests before you have the opportunity to meet her. We’ve got a quick summary below, so feel free to read each guide that we’ve linked:

  • A Study In Crimson - Help Vicho investigate murders to learn of Lacra’s whereabouts.
  • A Friend Like This - Meet Lacra and gain her trust.
  • Song of the Mountain - Travel with Lacra to the hidden Uriash Village and avoid hostilities.
  • A Mother’s Plea - Once you’re done with the above, chat with the uriash matriarch, Bakr-Erga.

The Blood of Dawnwalker A Mother’s Plea quest is where Bakr-Erga tells you about the village elders. She’s the last in line because her daughter, Ocha, is missing.

Where to find Ocha in Svartrau City

Your only clue if you want to find Ocha in The Blood of Dawnwalker is that she’s in one of the taverns in Svartrau City. You can ask around, or you could head directly to the tavern in Altmarkt. Talk to the bartender, who’ll tell you that Ocha is sitting in the corner.

When you chat with Ocha, she’ll get pissed off. You’ll be challenged to a fistfight. Win this bout to have a calmer talk with Ocha, as well as her friend, Nora.

It seems that the two have fallen in with a crime boss named Andrei. Your goal now is to check Andrei’s hideout so you can steal his memento. Ocha will then use her abilities to cast a hex on Andrei.

Go to the Alternmarkt tavern (left) and try not to get knocked out by Ocha (right).

How to enter Andrei’s hideout

This is where you start The Heart Wants What It Wants quest in The Blood of Dawnwalker. There are multiple options here, and various outcomes. Assuming you want to keep Ocha and Nora alive--and on good terms with you--you can try the following:

  • Go to the butcher’s shop, which is actually a front for Andrei’s illicit activities. Wait until it’s nighttime and use your vampiric powers to climb up the balcony.
  • If it’s still daytime, you can go to the butcher’s stall and activate Focus Mode. Look for a beggar who’s sitting on the street and pay him 50 denarii. Then, if you have any type of silver item in your inventory, talk to the butcher so you can enter the hideout.

Note 1: If you attempt to clamber onto the balcony during the day, the script of the NPCs inside the building will break. You won’t be able to progress this quest any further.

Note 2: If you go along with the butcher and present some silver, you’ll see Andrei who’s about to chop off a man’s arm. Stay silent and avoid any aggressive/hostile responses. If a fight breaks out and you end up killing Andrei, Ocha will be angry with you since you went against her plan.

You can either deal with the butcher (left) or climb up the balcony (right).

Which of Andrei’s mementos should you steal: Cleaver, pendant, or ring?

Okay, let’s say you’re inside Andrei’s hideout and you managed to avoid any fights so far. You can reply to Andrei with the following:

  • “Here’s what I’ve got.”
  • “Who wouldn’t be? What we’re doing here is illegal.”
  • “You know how to handle it, that’s for sure.”

These conciliatory responses will mollify Andrei. You’ll then have an opportunity to steal an item while he’s not looking. So, which among Andrei’s mementos should you get in The Blood of Dawnwalker?

  • The options are the cleaver, the pendant, and the ring.
  • The correct item is the ring. The hint comes from Andrei himself, who recalls a time when his father punched him so hard that the ring nearly caved in his skull.
  • This core memory is why the ring means so much to him, and why it’s the memento that Ocha should use for her hex.

How to save Nora

This is the next part of The Heart Wants What It Wants quest in The Blood of Dawnwalker. It occurs so quickly that it’s like it happened right under your nose:

  • Basically, once you grab the memento and leave Andrei’s hideout, you have to return to Ocha. This costs 2x Time Segments.
  • Ocha will inform you that Andrei’s goons kidnapped Nora. Yes, she’s now in the hideout that you just left.
  • Ocha, in a panic, wants to attack immediately, but there’s a risk that Nora might die due to the fighting. Instead, just tell her: “We should stick to the plan.”
  • Go back outside the building and activate Focus Mode. Walk over to the pigsty and choose [open the cage].
  • Once the guard gets distracted, peer through the ground-floor window. If you picked the ring as a memento, Ocha’s hex will succeed and Andrei will slam his head into the walls over and over. Looks like the crime boss got more than just a migraine.

How to make Ocha go home or stay in the city

This part concludes The Heart Wants What It Wants quest. You’ll have a chat with Ocha and your replies determine whether Ocha stays in the city or goes back to her tribe. First, tell her that you’d like to eat. Then, go to the river and catch 3x Crayfish. When you sit next to her by the campfire, you’ll trigger the conversation.

First choice:

  • “Do you miss home?” - Go back home.
  • “Do you like the city?” - Stay in the city.

Second choice:

  • “New things can be exciting, sure.” - Stay in the city.
  • “Meh. Nothing better than homemade food.” - Go back home.

Third choice:

  • “Our neighbors helped a bit” - Stay in the city.
  • “Other villagers just cared about themselves.” - Go back home.

If Andrei died via Ocha’s hex, she’ll be more inclined to stay in the city to become the new syndicate boss. However, if you pick all three “home” responses, she’ll return to her village. Likewise, you’ll receive 250 XP, 150 denarii, and the Broad Swing Manual for your efforts.

A Mother’s Plea: Conclusion and Ocha’s wares

Now that you’ve helped Ocha in The Blood of Dawnwalker, you can finish A Mother’s Plea. Return to the uriash matriarch and tell her the news. Regardless of Ocha’s decision, she’ll give you 250 XP, 150 denarii, and the Soul Stigma Manual.

As an aside, if Ocha decided to stay in the city, she and Nora will run Andrei’s syndicate. Pay her a visit and ask for her to train you:

  • You have to do a sparring match using weapons. This only happens once.
  • After beating Ocha, she’ll become a vendor. She mostly sells training manuals.
  • She also buys your silver items.

Report back to Ocha's mom (left) and buy some of Ocha's wares (right) if you want.

That does it for our guide on how to help Ocha in The Blood of Dawnwalker. Note that the uriash left behind glyphs all over Vale Sangora. If you haven’t discovered all of them yet, you can read our Pilgrimage for Power guide.

event_model_payload.headline: There’s A Legendary Herb In The Blood Of Dawnwalker That Permanently Increases Your Health
event_model_payload.summary:
Do you want to increase your character’s maximum health in The Blood of Dawnwalker? Survival is of the utmost importance, especially since you’ll be fighting against battalions of soldiers, hordes of undead, and cadres of vampiric hostiles. Thankfully, there’s a legendary herb that grants a one-time boon.

In This Article
  • The Hedgehog Herb and Razkovniche Plant guide 
    • The Hedgehog Herb - The dead alchemist and the ingredients
    • Waiting for the Razkovniche Plant to grow
    • How to craft the Razkovniche Elixir

The Hedgehog Herb and Razkovniche Plant guide 

The item that permanently increases your maximum health in The Blood of Dawnwalker is known as the Razkovniche Elixir. It’s a reward from a quest that’s aptly called The Hedgehog Herb. To start the quest, head over to the southern part of the world map, all the way to an abandoned settlement called Oghasti. It’s close enough to one of the Scouting Towers, too.

The Hedgehog Herb - The dead alchemist and the ingredients

Upon arriving at Oghasti, you’ll notice several houses in various states of disrepair. Inside one of the houses, there’s a corpse of a man. Activate Focus Mode and do the following:

  • Pick up or interact with objects like the seedbox and Razkovniche Potion recipe. There’s also a Watering Can outside the hut.
  • If it’s daytime, use your Astral Communion power to compel the spirit of the dead alchemist. Pick the Watering Can and the Razkovniche Potion Recipe so the spirit divulges more details.

Grab several items (left) and show them to the lost soul (right).

Waiting for the Razkovniche Plant to grow

For the next part of The Blood of Dawnwalker Hedgehog Herb quest, simply inspect the ceramic pot on the bench. Then, plant the Razkovniche Seed and give it a few drops of your blood. This costs 1x Time Segment.

You now have to wait for one full day to pass--i.e. if it’s currently noon (daytime at two pips), then you have to return the next noon. The plant will have grown by then, allowing you to harvest it. This also causes a Vidmo specter to spawn, so be sure to destroy it.

How to craft the Razkovniche Elixir

You have a couple of options to make the Razknovniche Elixir:

  • This can be crafted by Coen, though it requires 1x Time Segment.
  • Alternatively, you can return to Anca at the Crossroads Inn. She can then make the brew for you. This also costs 1x Time Segment.

That does it for our guide on how to complete The Hedgehog Herb in The Blood of Dawnwalker. The Razkovniche Elixir, once consumed, grants 20% maximum human health, 10% maximum vampiric health, and 1x skill point. This is a one-time boost, but it’s permanent.

event_model_payload.headline: How To Save Mert In The Blood Of Dawnwalker – The Firebrand Guide
event_model_payload.summary:
Are you looking for ways to save Mert in The Blood of Dawnwalker? This miller happens to be a cousin of one of Coen’s close friends. He might even be connected to a rebel group that’s planning to overthrow the vrakhiri overlords. Unfortunately, he’s rotting in a prison, but you have a chance to free him.

In This Article
  • The Firebrand quest guide - How to save Mert with the help of a few bugs
    • The Firebrand: Renna and the mill
    • The Firebrand: How to infiltrate Stoneward Post
    • Under Watchful Eyes: How to free Mert from the prison
    • Under Watchful Eyes: Escaping Stoneward Post
    • Shadows in the Woods: Sara, Crake, and Drogos
    • Where are Mert and Renna now?

The Firebrand quest guide - How to save Mert with the help of a few bugs

The Blood of Dawnwalker Firebrand quest becomes available quite early in the campaign:

  • The next morning after the Blood Mass, you check on the burned village of Laslea Glen. As you approach a corpse of a guard, you’ll see a banner in front of a ruined house.
  • The house once belonged to Coen’s friend, Vladimir, who has ties with the rebels.
  • Enter it and activate Focus Mode to look for clues. You should find a sack with silver arrowheads and a burnt letter.
  • Reading the letter kickstarts The Firebrand quest, which directs you to the home of a miller.

Note: Ideally, you should complete The Firebrand quest during the day. Since Coen is a human, there should be more options to converse with other NPCs. In our playthrough, however, we tackled these objectives at night. We did encounter a few bugs, which were helpful instead of being a hindrance.

The Firebrand: Renna and the mill

To do this part of The Firebrand quest in The Blood of Dawnwalker, go to the mill due south of Laslea Glen. You can’t miss it since it’s along the main road that’s dotted with fast travel shrines.

  • If you do this quest during the day, Mert’s wife, Renna, will greet you. She’ll tell you about her cart, which is a way for her to inform you that there are guards nearby and that Mert is already imprisoned inside the Stoneward Post. You can avoid fighting the guards at this stage.
  • At night, though, the guards will be alerted. You can lie to them about your identity, but you should still pick the “On second thought, talk to my sword about it.” Kill the guards and talk to Renna afterward. Ask her about Mert and she’ll tell you about Stoneward Post.

The Firebrand: How to infiltrate Stoneward Post

You can save Mert in The Blood of Dawnwalker if you play your cards right at this stage of The Firebrand quest. During the day:

  • The tasks are more involved, as you have to talk to several guards and NPCs.
  • All the back and forth eventually leads you to the overseer, and you can tell him that you’d like to see Mert.
  • You can pretend that Mert is “going to be sick,” which allows him to inform you about his manumit contact. This leads to another quest called Shadows in the Woods.
  • Also, now that you’ve met with Mert, you’ll be presented with a quest called Under Watchful Eyes. It’s time-sensitive, which means you only have a few days to break him out of prison. Failure to do so will lead to Mert’s death.

But if you do The Firebrand quest at night, you can utilize Coen’s vampiric abilities and traversal methods. Here’s what we did:

  • We went to the back of the tower in Stoneward Post. We had enough stamina to Shadowstep and Planeshift to reach the top.
  • We saved the game and gingerly dropped down the ledges, careful not to land on the floor.
  • There’s a slight opening where you can activate Focus Mode and target the overseer with Voracious Bite. Because the overseer is alone in the tower, you can fully drain his blood and kill him. Doing so lets you loot all sorts of items, including a key.
  • As an aside, if you accidentally land on the floor, the overseer will turn hostile and you have to fight him. He’ll likely kill Coen in a couple of hits.

You can sneak into Stoneward Post via the tower (left). But you can also accidentally fall and get spotted by the overseer (right).

Under Watchful Eyes: How to free Mert from the prison

Now, it’s time to do The Blood of Dawnwalker Under Watchful Eyes quest:

  • Use the key to open the door to the prison. Crouch-walk gingerly and activate Focus Mode as you approach the lone guard. Use Voracious Bite and drain him completely. You’ll also be able to loot the Prison Keychain from his corpse.
  • The dialogue here was actually bugged for us. It’s as though we were still exploring the area during the day--i.e. there was an option to talk to the guard even though he’s already dead.
  • That said, when we spoke with Mert a few times, we were eventually able to free him from his cell.

Grab the keys (left) and free Mert (right).

Under Watchful Eyes: Escaping Stoneward Post

The goal now is to save Mert in The Blood of Dawnwalker. If you read the quest description, it tells you that Mert has to pass through the Stoneward Post’s main gate. The problem is that there are four interconnected areas from the tower to the main gate, and they’re all filled with high-level soldiers.

Here’s how we managed this issue:

  • We went back up to the overseer’s room. There was a new fella named Rayko the Incorruptible. We used Voracious Bite until he pushed us away, then we just attacked and beat him normally. He dropped a Master Fencer Manual, along with other uncommon and rare loot.
  • Outside the overseer’s tower, we had to fight two soldiers and a dog. The encounter was still manageable since there was enough space in the yard.
  • We did not go to the other yards anymore. Instead, we checked the metal gate near the tower. The gate can be unlocked using the Prison Key, and the path actually leads to a somewhat hidden backdoor.

Since the coast was already clear, we simply told Mert to come with us to the backdoor exit. This allowed us to complete both The Firebrand and Under Watchful Eyes without too many hassles. We also suggested that Mert and Renna could go to the Svartrau City almshouse to seek sanctuary.

Note: If you still want to fight the other soldiers, you can obtain items like the Recipe for Supernatural’s Bane Brew, Swiftness Manual, and Restless Blade Manual.

Eliminate a few guards (left) and bring Mert to safety (right).

Shadows in the Woods: Sara, Crake, and Drogos

As mentioned earlier, this arc leads to another quest called Shadows in the Woods. Simply go to the marked location in the forest and you’ll spot a woman tied to a tree. Talk to the soldiers and either bribe them or take them out.

The woman, Sara, is a member of the Manumits. Follow her to be taken to the two leaders of the rebel group: Crake and Drogos. This unlocks an overarching quest called Where Loyalty Lies, where your goal is to increase your infamy to Notorious level or higher.

Rescue Sara (left) so you can meet the resistance deep in the woods (right).

Where are Mert and Renna now?

If you want to see Mert and Renna again, simply travel to Svartrau City. Go to the Cathedral Complex and enter the large building off to the side. You’ll find the couple resting on the second floor of the almshouse. They’ll thank Coen for his help.

That does it for our guide on how to save Mert in The Blood of Dawnwalker. He’s not the only character who needs aid. If you keep adventuring you might encounter folks with quests, such as Ocha: The Heart Wants What It Wants and Vicho: A Study In Crimson.

event_model_payload.headline: Should You Spare Isbrand In The Blood Of Dawnwalker – Our Rotten Roots Guide
event_model_payload.summary:
Are you thinking of whether you should abandon or spare Isbrand in The Blood of Dawnwalker? This ancient vampire lord has been around for centuries, though he’s been left in a weakened state. Maybe he can aid you in the battles ahead? Oh, and before we continue, please know that this guide contains spoilers.

In This Article
  • Our Rotten Roots quest guide - Should you spare or abandon Isbrand
    • Anachora and the Isbrand boss fight
    • Should you invite Isbrand in?

Our Rotten Roots quest guide - Should you spare or abandon Isbrand

The Blood of Dawnwalker Our Rotten Roots quest is actually part of a very long story arc involving the vampiress Lacra. For starters, you meet her during A Friend Like This. That’s followed by Song of the Mountain, where you travel with her to a hidden Uriashi Village.

She’ll then ask you to help her find Isbrand during Hive and Seek. Your delve deep underground culminates in a massive battle against hordes of kobolds and their larger kin. Once all the hostiles have been eliminated, you can check one of the chests nearby to obtain Isbrand’s Plate, a legendary medium chestpiece that grants maximum vampiric health, claw critical hit chance, claw critical hit damage, and blood drinking restoration.

Anachora and the Isbrand boss fight

Coen and Lacra then take Isbrand’s near-lifeless carcass to Westridge Outpost. After a day has passed, you can tackle the Our Rotten Roots quest. It involves diving into Isbrand’s memories, entering a realm called Anachora:

  • In the third major area, you’ll see a fork in the road. Lacra does not want you to head to the left, as she wants to keep her past a secret. If you continue there, you’ll learn about the grievous harm that Isbrand caused. You can also apologize to Lacra later.
  • At the end of the sequence, you have to fight Isbrand, with Lacra as your ally. Isbrand has erratic attack patterns, so try to block or dodge his blows if you can.
  • He also casts Piercing Shriek at a wide frontal cone.

Should you invite Isbrand in?

After the bout, you can decide on what you have to do with Isbrand in The Blood of Dawnwalker. Initially, Lacra will tell Isbrand to beg, as she might want to spare him if you say nothing. However, you can choose the following replies:

  • “Beg for what?”
  • “Can I do it instead?”

This leads to two choices:

  • “I’ll do it. I invite you in, Isbrand.” - This allows Coen to gain Isbrand’s essence or soul.
  • “I’m sorry. You’ll stay here, forever.” - Isbrand’s soul will be left to rot in Anachora for all eternity.

If you decide to invite him in, he’ll sometimes speak to Coen, although the voice is only in his head. It’s a cool feature that’s thematic for the game, and it can be done for other vampire lords that you vanquish, too. Oh, and regardless of your decision, you’ll receive the Piercing Shriek ability as a reward.

That does it for our The Blood of Dawnwalker Isbrand guide. Since we’ve already mentioned Piercing Shriek, you might want to know about the best perks and abilities for each skill tree. Likewise, since Our Rotten Roots is part of a story arc, you might want to learn about how you can romance Lacra.

event_model_payload.headline: How To Help Father Florin In The Blood Of Dawnwalker – Hero’s End Guide
event_model_payload.summary:
Are you hoping to help Father Florin in The Blood of Dawnwalker? This wily priest hasn’t been around since the prologue. If you do manage to find him, then he has a proposal that might pique your interest. Of course, he also has his ulterior motives. Our guide has all the details that you need as we discuss several quests, including In the Name of the Father, Hero’s End, and Champion of Old. By the time you’re done with these activities, you should have at least four legendary items.

In This Article
  • Father Florin story arc: In the Name of the Father and Hero’s End
    • Detour time: The Treasury
    • In the Name of the Father: Should you help Father Florin or kill him?
    • Hero’s End: The Hand of Fate
    • Hero’s End: The Strange Mural
    • Hero’s End: The Ancient Hero’s Armor
    • Champion of Old: Erka’s Sword

Father Florin story arc: In the Name of the Father and Hero’s End

Before you can help Father Florin in The Blood of Dawnwalker, you must first ascertain his location. If you haven’t done so yet, make your way to Svartrau City in the middle of the world map. Then, head over to the large cathedral that dwarfs the other buildings.

If you enter during the day, you’ll see Father Florin in the middle of a sermon, where he’s baptizing a baby with blood. Gross!

Florin does confide in you that he has a scheme. He then tells you to meet him in his hideout, which gets marked on your map. This kickstarts the In the Name of the Father quest.

Detour time: The Treasury

Since you’re already in the cathedral, you might as well explore for a bit:

  • Walk to the main entrance and talk to the acolyte. Ask for his help in opening the storage room. This costs 1x Time Segment.
  • Inspect the objects inside the room and grab the Treasury Key from the journal.
  • Exit the cathedral and use the Treasury Key to unlock the building on the opposite side of the courtyard.

The young acolyte (left) can help you get the Treasure Key (right).

You can pick up a bunch of goodies inside the Treasury Building:

  • The Recipe for Potent Vitality Balm is inside a container on the first floor.
  • Go to the room on the second floor and take the Recipe for Potent Balm of Fortitude.
  • The same room has a Phial of Xanthe’s Blood. This is a legendary consumable that automatically teaches you the Blood Surge ability.
  • Check the first floor and move the shelf. Go down the ladder to the cellar and take the Recipe for Powder of Sharp Mind.
  • Don’t forget to grab the Stone Key from the altar. You’ll need it for a chest in the location where you’re headed soon.

In the Name of the Father: Should you help Father Florin or kill him?

It’s time to continue the In the Name of the Father quest in The Blood of Dawnwalker. Go to the back of the building in the marked location and enter through the doorway. When you drop down the basement, you’ll realize that there’s a long-forgotten temple complex. Looks like Florin and his cohorts have made a shocking discovery.

Head to the inner chamber and have a chat with Florin. You have several options here:

  • You can agree to his plan since you need help stopping Brencis. This leads to the next quest, Hero’s End.
  • You can kill him outright. He’ll drop the Ancient Key that opens the door to the ruins, which will still allow you to do the Hero’s End quest. That said, you have to fight his other recruits.
  • You can also refuse to deal with him any further.

Hero’s End: The Hand of Fate

Okay, let’s say you want to help Father Floring in The Blood of Dawnwalker. Naturally, you want to keep him alive, too. Just head through the door unlocked by the Ancient Key and make your way deeper into the forgotten ruins. There are two legendary items for you to find, as well as an important object that you must examine.

First, make your way to the left until you see a chamber with a pit that has a greenish glow. Use your Planeshift to drop down the cavern and traverse the area. You’ll reach a small room guarded by several Hive Kobolds. Kill all of them and use the Stone Key from earlier to unlock the chest.

This nets you The Hand of Fate, a legendary sword that grants Witchcraft ability cooldown, Witchcraft ability damage, Activation Charge restoration (actions), and Activation Charge restoration (passive). Next, check the shallow pit with the ladder and take the Old Key. It opens a nearby door that leads you back to the temple complex.

The chasm with the green glow (left) leads you to a niche with a legendary item (right).

Hero’s End: The Strange Mural

For this part of the Hero’s End quest in The Blood of Dawnwalker, you need to look for a strange mural in one of the connecting rooms. It’s just an optional task, but inspecting it is important.

Once you do this, you’ll receive a side quest called Champion of Old, as well as the Decrepit Key. You can tackle this objective much later.

Hero’s End: The Ancient Hero’s Armor

The main goal in The Blood of Dawnwalker Hero’s End quest is the acquisition of an armor believed to have been blessed. When you arrive in the main chamber, you’ll battle a miniboss called Rigoz, the Betrayed Hero, who’s surrounded by a bunch of lowly mobs. Eliminate the enemies and check out the loot:

  • Soul Stigma Manual
  • Recipe for Potent Balm of Fortitude
  • Ancient Hero’s Armor - This legendary heavy chestpiece has human health restoration, Witchcraft ability damage, damage against supernatural enemies, and Activation Charge restoration (actions).

Oh, and if you squeeze through the gap, you’ll find a corpse with the Simple Key. Use it to open the door at the top of the steps. This gives you a shortcut back to the initial area.

When you’re done, return to Father Florin and tell him that you’ve succeeded. For your efforts, you’ll receive not just 250 XP, but also a way to infiltrate Greifberg Castle. Florin will inform you about a secret knock sequence that allows you to enter the courtyard. Note that this method lets you enter the citadel on your own during the day, as opposed to climbing up the walls at night.

Champion of Old: Erka’s Sword

One last thing: Make sure you’re tracking the Champion of Old quest and go to the marked location on the map. If you cut through the vines, you’ll spend 3x Time Segments. Inside, loot some of the stuff, including a Soul Stigma Manual. Then, inspect the other murals.

After inspecting all the murals, a miniboss named Erkas the Repenter will emerge. He’s your typical Forgotten Warrior archetype, so he shouldn’t pose too much of a threat. Defeating him nets you Erka’s Sword, a legendary weapon that has maximum human health, weapon critical hit chance, weapon critical damage, and damage against supernatural enemies.

That does it for our guide on how to help Father Florin in The Blood of Dawnwalker. With all these legendaries, you might be raring to rush Brencis’ citadel. Of course, if you need more powerful gear, you probably want to obtain the Sword of St. Mihai, too.

event_model_payload.headline: All Sword Shard Locations In The Blood Of Dawnwalker – Forge It Anew Guide
event_model_payload.summary:
Are you searching for all the Sword Shards in The Blood of Dawnwalker? These items are necessary if you want to complete the Forge It Anew quest. With these, you’ll be able to create one of the best weapons in the entire game.

In This Article
  • Forge It Anew - All Sword Shards in Vale Sangora
    • Forge It Anew: Do Not Disturb
    • Forge It Anew: Executive Order
    • Forge It Anew: Hostile Takeover
    • The Uriash Blacksmith
    • The final trial for the Sword of St. Mihai

Forge It Anew - All Sword Shards in Vale Sangora

The Blood of Dawnwalker Forge It Anew quest isn’t available right from the get-go. You actually need to explore a bit just to make it appear in your journal:

  • One method is to visit any of the three caves that we discuss in detail below. Each cave has a mural that depicts the landscape of the valley. Inspecting it reveals the other locations on the world map.
  • The other option is tied to a different side quest called A Monk and a Saint. You obtain a broken weapon and you learn that shards are needed to reforge it.

Note: Trying to obtain each shard requires 3x Time Segments.

Forge It Anew: Do Not Disturb

The first Sword Shard in The Blood of Dawnwalker comes from the Do Not Disturb sub-quest. You have to go just a bit north of the Maragir Wealds marker on the world map.

From the marked location, you’ll see a large and slanted rock formation. Pass underneath it and follow the path until you stumble upon a pack of kobolds. Kill them as you see fit, and enter the cavern to eliminate more hostile creatures. Once the coast is clear, pick up the shard from the nest.

Head past the rock formation (left) and finish off the pack of kobolds (right).

Forge It Anew: Executive Order

There’s another kobold cave further southeast in the ridges near Tantari. However, once you get there, you’ll realize that Xanthe’s soldiers have killed all the creatures. Read the note to learn that the soldiers have taken their plunder to a camp due southwest of Tantari.

Scout the camp first from a higher vantage point. There are several guards in this place, and trying to fight them all can be very challenging indeed. Thankfully, there’s a way to “cheese” this encounter:

  • Bear in mind that the Sword Shard is inside the main tent in the middle of the camp.
  • Go to one of the camp’s edges, preferably along the northern side. Attack one of the soldiers to lure everyone up the sloping path.
  • While doing so, you might “aggro” a bunch of wild boar that, in turn, would attack the guards, too.
  • While everyone is busy, sprint and circle around the swamps. You should “drop aggro” as you move away, which means you can enter the tent to grab the item. Do this quickly before any of your foes walks back into the camp.

You need access to the main tent (left), so try to lure all the enemies until they're outside the camp (right).

Forge It Anew: Hostile Takeover

This part of the Forge It Anew quest in The Blood of Dawnwalker requires you to travel southwest of Boar’s Back. Just past the Giant’s Pawns shrine, there’s a cave that’s become a kobold nest. However, the resident isn’t just a mere kobold. It’s actually a Wrongs variant miniboss called Munch-Munch.

This type of creature has deadly attacks that inflict poison. Its claw swipes and breath spew abilities inflict this debilitating debuff. Try to block and dodge everything to survive the battle. When your opponent is dead, claim the Sword Shard from the nest.

The Uriash Blacksmith

Now that you’ve found all the Sword Shards in The Blood of Dawnwalker, it’s time to look for the one person who can actually work on the materiel. It’s none other than a lone uriash blacksmith northwest of Briar Sloughs.

Note: To clarify, the Sword Shards themselves aren’t enough. You still need to find the broken sword and its hilt. You can learn more about this in our A Monk and a Saint quest guide.

The northwestern hinterlands (left) is where the uriash blacksmith resides (right).

The final trial for the Sword of St. Mihai

Let’s say you’ve already found the broken sword, well, just hand over all the quest items to the uriash blacksmith. She’ll then craft the Restored Sword of St. Mihai, an epic-tier weapon. But why stop there?

The blacksmith will then tell you that you can improve the weapon further. Go up the slope to the northwest until you see an opening that’s covered in red vines and use your sword to cut through the obstacles. Inside, you’ll find yourself in a cavernous area with lots of dryad-like undead. Continue to the innermost chamber and inspect the altar.

When you’re ready, perform the ritual and spend 3x Time Segments. This begins one of the most arduous encounters in the entire game, one that has multiple enemy waves. All your foes are undead variants and it’s a slog to take them all out. But if you succeed, you’ll acquire the legendary Imbued Sword of St. Mihai.

This legendary weapon grants Swordmastery ability cooldown, weapon critical hit chance, weapon critical hit damage, and damage against supernatural enemies. The weapon art also hits a wide area. Oh, and you also unlock the “Arbiter’s Blade” achievement for your troubles.

That does it for our guide on how to complete the Forge It Anew quest in The Blood of Dawnwalker. You now have one of the best legendary items in the game, but if you’re looking for more, you might want to tackle Father Florin’s quest chain. Upon completing all related objectives, you should have four legendary items, including one that teaches a special Vampiric ability.

event_model_payload.headline: How To Repair St. Mihai’s Sword In The Blood Of Dawnwalker
event_model_payload.summary:
Are you trying to repair St. Mihai’s Sword in The Blood of Dawnwalker? This armament was once wielded by a renowned warrior, who was eventually canonized by the church. Now, it lays forgotten deep underground. If you’re up to the task, then you might claim it as your own. Oh, and before we continue, please be reminded that this article contains minor spoilers.

In This Article
  • A Monk and a Saint - The Sword of Saint Mihai quest line
    • Albertus’ location and riddle
    • Night Terrors and St. Mihai’s memorial stone
    • The St. Mihai boss fight

A Monk and a Saint - The Sword of Saint Mihai quest line

To obtain the Sword of St. Mihai in The Blood of Dawnwalker, you have to complete a quest called A Monk and a Saint. But before you can even start it, you must tackle Anca’s Echoes of Silenced Bells quest. She’ll then divulge the location of a monk named Albertus.

Albertus’ location and riddle

The Blood of Dawnwalker Monk and a Saint quest requires you to head to the Middens. It’s the slums in the western outskirts of Svartrau City. The place is crawling with undead dogs, so watch out.

Also, keep your eyes peeled for glyphs on walls. Keep Focus Mode active until you see a house that’s covered entirely in glyphs. Inside, you’ll find Albertus who seems to be in an addled state.

Your goal now is to provide the correct responses about St. Mihai’s legend. Here are the right answers:

  • Abelard the Sorrowful
  • Svartrau Plaza
  • His penance, the place of his redemption
  • Never once set foot inside it
  • St. Mihai, a great warrior, arrived at Vale Sangora

Thank Albertus for his help. Don’t forget to pick up the Herbal Remedies I Manual from the pile of discarded stuff.

Night Terrors and St. Mihai’s memorial stone

Next up if you want the Sword of St. Mihai in The Blood of Dawnwalker, you must go to the cathedral’s courtyard.

  • Investigate the well, which requires 1x Time Segment. Down below, you’ll spot a bunch of kobolds. Take them out as you see fit.
  • There’s a corpse next to a wall. Investigate this scene and use up 1x Time Segment. You’ll learn about St. Mihai’s memorial stone in the courtyard.
  • Head back topside and go to the garden with the stone cross.
  • While facing the cross, interact with the third memorial stone from the left. Coen will move the block, revealing a hidden passageway. This action costs 1x Time Segment.

Investigate the tunnels beneath the well to discover a clue about St. Mihai's crypt.

The St. Mihai boss fight

You now have to fight St. Mihai himself in the catacombs. He has rapid, unblockable attacks whenever he lunges. He also covers the area in a thick fog, and he follows through with a flanking strike.

With Mihai defeated, you can go ahead and loot the, uh, Broken Sword of St. Mihai. And if it’s still daytime, you can compel Mihai’s spirit. Pick up the Worn Sheathe and the Broken Chains to learn about what truly happened to him.

That does it for our guide on how to get the Sword of St. Mihai in The Blood of Dawnwalker. This entire quest nets you a whopping 1,000 XP and an extra skill point. As for the weapon itself, it’s actually next to useless at its current state. But if you want to see its true potential, you have to collect a few special items known as Sword Shards. From there, you can temper the weapon until it reaches legendary tier. We’ve got all the details for you in our Forge It Anew quest guide.

event_model_payload.headline: Onimusha: Way of the Sword is best when it's silly, and despite some gloomy open world slogging, sometimes even remembers it
event_model_payload.summary:
The opening minutes of Onimusha: Way of the Sword are glorious, in the sense that they’re utterly shambolic. Wandering ronin Musashi wakes up under a bridge, belts a wrong-footingly British "WOT?!" at some starving urchins eyeing up his rice ball, then proceeds to be chased around a muddy village by what feels like two thousand martial arts students, only occasionally stopping to boot a wooden plank into their faces or scoop up an imperilled dog. It’s goofy and brash and genuinely funny, in a way that immediately looks to elevate it among the field of po-faced fantasy slashers as effectively as any well-honed parry mechanic.

Why in the following hours, then, does Way of the Sword make only occasional attempts to match this intro’s energy?
